strategy.summary:
Kohlering-Technik Pirkheim is a sound, family-owned seal maker (credit index flat, VDA 6.3 A). We are a small customer to it, about 0.8 % of its turnover. It supplies two dual-sourced parts under a framework agreement with prices fixed per calendar year.

The two parts call for opposite approaches.
- Part 340011 (mechanical seal): it is our cheaper source. Its price sits about 8 % above our should-cost. It has recently put standard mechanical seals on allocation (news:20260827-25), and its delivery on this part is weak. Here we need supply security: a moderate stance plus volume and length.
- Part 340040 (lip seal): it is about 10 % dearer than Elasto-Dicht (sup:70430). It has the worse ppm and two open 8Ds. This is our real price lever.

How it negotiates:
- It states that only multi-year volume agreements change prices (doc:20260910-70440-M1).
- Moves above 2 % need a pricing committee that meets every two weeks (doc:20260524-70440-M2).
- It historically settles far below its ask.

No cash stress is visible.
strategy.decision_maker: Key account manager (authority up to about 2 % on price) backed by a pricing committee meeting fortnightly for larger changes; day-to-day contact is a new inside-sales colleague since Oct 2025 with likely limited authority.

persona.style: Rule-bound and firm on list prices ('standard items are not discounted'). Moves through structured deals (multi-year, volume) and settles near its committee threshold.
other_traits: allocating mechanical seals on prior-year call-offs
we are a small customer (about 0.8 % of turnover)

needs.detail: It wants multi-year, binding volume agreements and says this is the only route to price changes.
It is allocating standard mechanical seals on last year's call-offs. Our delivery record on 340011 is poor, so it likely values predictable call-offs and realistic lead times.
Our forecasts for both parts are rising and have been shared with it. Firm volume is valued, especially on the lip seal, where it risks losing quota.
Labour and rubber indices are at their 36-month peak. It may seek recovery or an index link on 340040, which is rubber-heavy.

Allocation of standard mechanical seals means 340011 growth may not be served without an agreement.
Prices are fixed per calendar year and changes need 90 days' notice before year end. The contract auto-extends 12 months unless notice is given.
It refuses discounts on standard items outside multi-year volume deals.

Shows its 340011 price already carries margin. Use it to deflect an increase, not to force a deep cut, given allocation.
Forecast growth on the mechanical seal. A secured allocation in return for a binding volume is worth more than a price cut.
It has repeatedly settled near zero. Use this to anchor expectations on any increase ask.
Same point for the mechanical seal.
Eight supplier-caused complaints on the lip seal, with 8Ds still open. A fresh fact to justify our price position or a ppm commitment.
On-time delivery is far below the contract target and the peer median. Use it as a later fresh fact, not as the main lever.
Annual fixed prices with a notice requirement. Use it if a late or mid-year increase is asked.
Confirms the 340040 gap. Use it only if the case lists that quote.
We are a reliable payer, though slightly late. Mention it only if payment is raised, and pair it with a commitment to pay on time.

trades.why: It explicitly links price movement to multi-year agreements. 24 months captures most of the value.
Binding volume within our real need answers its allocation logic and its stated pricing rule.
It is capacity-strained on mechanical seals. Accepting its standard lead time avoids a steep premium and supports reliable supply.
There is no cash need, so faster payment buys little. Asking for long payment would cost price. Keep the current terms and promise to pay on time.
On 340040 its quality is worse than the rival's. A tighter ppm target is a fair ask from a supplier wanting to keep its quota.
Rubber and labour indices are at their peaks. Avoid a clause unless it insists on one for a long term, and then price the risk carefully.

price_view.reasoning: There is real room on 340040, where the rival is about 10 % cheaper and has better quality. On 340011 there is little room: the price is near a healthy margin over should-cost, it beats the rival, and allocation gives it the upper hand. Its index-driven case is modest and already covered by the last increase on 340011.

Long payment terms requested together with a price cut will stall it.

strategy.writer_notes: Treat the two parts differently. - Lip seal: lead with the rival's current price and a binding multi-year volume offer. Back it with the quality record as a later fresh fact. - Mechanical seal: aim to hold the price or accept a small step. Secure an allocation covering our forecast growth in exchange for binding volume and a longer term. Keep individual requested moves within its key account manager's authority where possible so it can close quickly. Expect its first counter to carry most of the concession. Answer every round. Note: evidence on its personal negotiating style is thin, and there is no should-cost for the lip seal.

findings.text: Part 340011: price EUR 37.55 sits +8.1% above our bottom-up should-cost of EUR 34.74, which already includes overhead but no margin. That is a modest, roughly healthy margin, not an excessive one. Confidence is about ±5%, so realistic room for a cut from cost alone is small, around 0-3%.

Part 340011 drivers: labour (weight 0.33) rose +2.7% and rubber PPI (weight 0.17) rose +3.9% over 12 months. Together they imply about +1.5% on price. The 2026-01 increase of +2.1% already covers more than that. A further rise is not justified now. Both indices are at their 36-month peak, so they give no argument for a decrease either.

Part 340011 competitive position: Kohlering is the cheaper of our two sources. It charges 37.55, while Ravensteiner (sup:70410) charges 38.29. Kohlering also won the 2024 benchmark RFQ at 40.23 against Ravensteiner's 41.55. The rival price argues for them, not for us, so we should not cite it.

Part 340040: Kohlering charges 111.69 per 100. The alternative source Elasto-Dicht (sup:70430) charges 100.98, so Kohlering is about 10.6% dearer. In the 2025 RFQ, Kohlering quoted 121.27 against 102.34 and lost. Its lead time was also much longer, 36 days against 7. This is the strongest price lever with this supplier: there is room of around 8-10% to match the market.

Part 340040 drivers: rubber PPI (weight 0.54, +3.9%) and labour (weight 0.12, +2.7%) imply about +2.4% on price. Kohlering held its price flat in 2026 after +1.8% in 2025, so it may claim this. The claim is outweighed by the 10% gap to the competitor. We have no should-cost for 340040, so the evidence on its margin is thin.

Market news that Kohlering might use (copper +48%, electronic boards +41%, steel +7.3%) is not among its weighted drivers for these seals. Industrial power prices are -43% on 2022, which argues against energy-based claims.

findings.text: Decision structure: the key account manager can only move up to 2 % on his own. Larger price changes go to a pricing committee that meets every two weeks. Any ask or concession above 2 % adds up to two weeks of latency. Packaging moves inside 2 % lets them close fast.

Stated stance: standard items are not discounted; only multi-year volume agreements change prices. Their lever is commitment length and binding volume, not argument alone. A multi-year term sheet is the door to price movement.

Capacity red flag: since 2026-08 they allocate standard mechanical seals in line with last year's call-offs. Our planned increases (part 340011: 12,720 vs 11,420; part 340040: 39,100 vs 37,200) may not be served without an agreement. This gives them supply leverage.

Financially sound, stable family-owned GmbH: 35.2 M EUR turnover, equity ratio 24.5 %, credit index flat at 147, VDA 6.3 grade A. There is no cash stress to exploit, and they can walk away. We are about 0.8 % of their turnover, a small customer.
Our payment behaviour: average 3 days late and 86.7 % of invoices late, though never more than 9 days. They may raise this. Paying on time or faster at 30 days is a cheap concession we could trade.
Contact change: inside sales took over our account in October 2025. The working contact may have limited authority, so the key account manager and committee are the real decision makers.
Evidence on their personal style and specific complaints is thin. No letters from them asking for increases appear in the record.

findings.text: Framework agreement ctr:4600070440 covers both parts (340011 mechanical seal, 340040 lip seal), runs 2025-07-01 to 2027-06-30 and auto-extends 12 months unless terminated with 90 days' notice (by 2027-04-01). Prices are fixed per calendar year; a change needs written notice at least 90 days before year end, so by about 2026-10-02 for a 2027 change. A notice arriving later cannot change the 2027 price under the contract.

Commercial terms favour the supplier: payment is 30 days net against our 60-day standard, delivery is DAP with a 35-day lead time, and the quality agreement sets a 95% on-time target and a EUR 150 flat fee per supplier-caused complaint. Moving payment toward 60 days is a lever, or a currency we can trade.

It settles well below what it asks. On 340011 it asked 2.9/1.1/4.8% and settled 0/0/2.1%. On 340040 it asked 3.9/4.7/1.7% and settled 0/1.8/0%. In the last 3 years each part took only one increase. The 2% pricing-committee threshold matches settlements that stay at or near 2%.

Both parts are dual-sourced. On 340011 it holds 60% and Ravensteiner (sup:70410) 40%; it won the 2024 benchmark RFQ (rfq:6000000117), and the rival's current price is about 2% higher, so our leverage there is limited. On 340040 the quota is split 50/50 with Elasto-Dicht (sup:70430), which won the 2025 benchmark (rfq:6000000119) and is currently about 9.6% cheaper, giving us strong leverage to shift quota. Tooling owner is recorded as n/a in sourcing, while the argument library says it owns tooling; this contradiction is unresolved.

Mutual dependency is low. Our spend of EUR 288k is about 0.8% of its EUR 35.2M turnover, the company is financially sound (credit index 147 unchanged), and it is allocating mechanical seal volumes on last year's call-offs. For 340011 it has the upper hand on supply; on 340040 we can walk.

findings.text: Delivery is weak and getting worse: rolling OTD against requested date 75.5% (Q3 2026) vs 77.6% a year earlier and 81.5% peak in 2025Q2; against its own confirmed date only 79.2%. The target is 95% and the peer median is 84.6%. Late lines average 12.1 days late, with a maximum of 21. The 'class A green' label hides a 20-point gap to the contract target.

Lateness is concentrated on mechanical seal part:340011: 65.4% on time requested and 73.1% confirmed, with 34.6% of lines late (avg 13.3 days). Lip seal part:340040 runs at 85.2%. The 35-day lead time on 340011 plus lateness pushes us to buffer stock.

Quality is drifting up: rolling ppm 294 a year ago, now 387, with complaints rising from 7 to 10. It is still below the peer median of 457 ppm, and no 8Ds are overdue, so overall quality partly argues its case.

Part:340040 is the quality problem. It had 8 supplier-caused QNs in 12 months, covering coating, dimension, leakage at test, wrong certificate, burr and surface damage, and 2 are still without a closed 8D. Its 12-month ppm of 429 is worse than rival sup:70430 at 338, which is also about 9.6% cheaper. Part:340011 is better: 279 ppm vs rival sup:70410 at 218, with 2 supplier-caused QNs in 12 months.

The volume outlook is up and has been shared with the supplier. For part:340011 the forecast is 12,720 for the next 12 months vs 11,420 ordered (+11%). For part:340040 it is 39,100 vs 37,200 (+5%). Forecasts have been stable, which makes them credible as a basis for a multi-year volume agreement. The supplier has stated that only such agreements change its prices.

Price history: part:340011 rose from 36.77 to 37.55 (+2.1%). Part:340040 rose from 109.71 to 111.69 per 100 (+1.8%), against rival sup:70430 at 100.98. Recent orders were confirmed on the requested dates, with one exception at +8 days on the 340040 line.

arguments.text: On the mechanical seal 340011 we are already your cheaper source, and we have been for years. We are at 37.55 against Ravensteiner's 38.29. We held 36.77 flat for three years (2023-2025) and settled 2026 at only +2.1 % against a 4.8 % ask. In the 2024 benchmark we also won at 40.23 against 41.55.

Our costs are at their 36-month peak. Rubber products PPI is +3.9 % year on year and manufacturing labour +2.7 %, with labour about a third of the seal cost. Your own should-cost of 34.74 carries no margin, so 37.55 leaves only about 8 %. That is thin for a 140-person family firm with a 24.5 % equity ratio.

Standard mechanical seals are on allocation, based on last year's call-offs. Your forecast for 340011 is up to 12,720 pcs, against roughly 11,420 ordered. We can only secure that growth inside a binding multi-year volume agreement. That is also the only route by which prices move, as we stated on 10 September.

Under the contract, prices are fixed per calendar year. The framework runs to 2027-06 and extends automatically. Any change needs 90 days' notice, and anything above 2 % has to go to our pricing committee.
On the lip seal we have kept price changes small: 0 % in 2024 (asked 3.9 %), +1.8 % in 2025, and 0 % in 2026. Rubber, which is about half of that part's cost, has since risen 3.9 %.

Our commercial and quality record is solid. We hold VDA 6.3 grade A, ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, a stable credit index, scorecard class A green throughout, no overdue 8Ds, and full payment of the EUR 150 chargebacks.

weak_points: Delivery on 340011 is poor. Only 65.4 % arrived on time to the requested date in the last 12 months, with an average 13 days late, and the scorecard OTD of 75.5 % is far below the contractual 95 % target.
The lip seal 340040 is about 10.6 % dearer than Elasto-Dicht (111.69 vs 100.98). We lost the 2025 benchmark heavily: 121.27 with a 36-day lead time against their 102.34 with 7 days.
Lip seal ppm is 429, against 338 at Elasto-Dicht. Two 8Ds are still open (qn:20005017, qn:20005029), and complaints are recurring: dimensions, wrong certificates, coating.
Ppm on the 340011 part is also worse than Ravensteiner's (279 vs 218).
The scorecard trend is falling: 88.6 down to 85.8, with complaints rising to 10.
Our cost argument is thin. Steel is not a material driver for us, power prices are down 43 % on 2022, and the 2026 increase on 340011 already absorbed part of the index rise.
We are a small customer relationship for them: about 0.8 % of our turnover, and both parts are dual-sourced, so they can shift quota.
wants: A binding 24-36 month volume agreement covering both parts. In return: price stability on 340011, and possibly a step down on 340040 toward about 105-107.
Higher quota on 340040, ideally 60 % or more, plus firm call-off schedules, in return for a lip seal price cut.
Payment at 30 days kept or shortened. They currently pay about 3 days late on average; we would trade a small concession for punctual or shorter payment.
A rubber index clause on 340040 as an alternative to fixed-price absorption.
A guaranteed 340011 allocation tied to forecast commitment, at the current price.
A realistic lead time on 340011 written into the agreement, around 35-42 days, instead of disputes over the 95 % OTD target.
red_lines: No price reduction on 340011 below about 37.0. Margin over cost is already thin, and they are not getting volume beyond allocation without a commitment.
No discounts on standard items without a multi-year volume commitment.
No unilateral changes to fixed annual prices outside the contract's notice rules.
No chargeback above EUR 150 per complaint, and no ppm commitment that is not matched by a price adjustment.
No lip seal cut deeper than about 5 % without quota or volume in return.
red_team.opening: Thank you for the forecast update; we welcome the growth. On the mechanical seal 340011 we have been your most cost-effective source for years. With rubber at +3.9 % and labour at +2.7 %, both at 36-month highs, we cannot reduce, and we would ask for a modest adjustment of about 2.5 %. Because standard mechanical seals are currently allocated on last year's call-offs, we suggest securing your higher 12,720 pcs through a 24-month volume agreement covering both seals. Within such an agreement we would be prepared to review the lip seal 340040 price, and to agree a delivery plan for 340011 that we can reliably meet.

rebuttals.answer: We value that you have been a competitive source on the mechanical seal, and we have rewarded that with the larger share of the volume. A competitive position is the basis of that share, though, not a reason for an increase. The current price is our anchor, and it has not fallen at any point over the period. Your own history also shows that renewals settle well below the opening ask, and we expect the same realism this time.

The two indices you name are real, and we accept that they have risen. Weighted by their share of the seal's cost, together they support well under the increase you are asking for. The last renewal already absorbed part of that rise. Our bottom-up estimate of your plant shows the current price already carries a margin above cost. Your financial standing is stable and sound, so we see no case for recovery beyond the weighted index effect. Energy, a large cost for many producers, has fallen sharply over recent years.

We hear you on allocation, and we are ready to give you exactly what you asked for: a binding multi-year volume agreement. Our forecast has been shared with you and shows growth on both parts. In return, we expect that agreement to secure allocation for our full forecast and to be reflected in price, as your own rule describes. Growing, committed volume is worth more to you, not less.

Agreed, the contract fixes prices per calendar year and requires notice. That works in both directions: it protects the current prices until a properly notified change has been agreed. We will respect your committee cycle. For that reason we propose an agreement your account manager can close within his authority wherever possible.

We acknowledge your restraint on the lip seal and the rise in rubber prices. However, our approved second source supplies the same part today at a clearly lower price. It also offered a much shorter lead time in the last benchmark. For you to keep or grow your share on this part, the price needs to move toward the market level. Holding it or raising it would not achieve that.

The operational record, however, is weaker than the labels suggest. On-time delivery stays far below the contractual target and below the peer median. We would welcome a ppm and delivery commitment as part of the new agreement.
